title: I'm a solo dev and I built a game with Claude where you draw a roller coaster with your finger, then ride it
author: javiergame4
selftext:
Hey everyone, I'm a solo indie dev (One Life Studios) and I just released **RideForge** on iPhone. I built it in Unity with Claude as my coding partner, and I wanted to share how that went along with the game.

**The game:** you draw the track, then you ride it. Sketch a line and it becomes a coaster. Keep it tame or make it completely insane, then hop in and see if it survives.

🎢 Loops, corkscrews, huge drops and underwater tunnels  
🌍 4 worlds: Sunset Canyon, Frosty Peaks, Tropical Island and Neon City  
👥 Ride Together with up to 4 friends  
🎰 Ride Roulette: get dropped onto a random coaster someone else made  
🌐 Community rides: play, like and follow other creators  
🏗️ Build your own theme park, plus a Daily Ride  
🕹️ Arcade and Simulation modes  
Free with optional ads, and a one-time $3.99 removes them.

**How I built it with Claude:**  
I'm one person, so Claude did a lot of the heavy lifting. I used it to:  
• write and debug the Unity C# code (track drawing, ride physics, multiplayer, community rides)  
• set up the online features with Unity Gaming Services  
• fix App Store review rejections (account deletion, the tracking prompt)  
• make the trailer, App Store screenshots and previews  
• write the privacy policy and support pages

It's not magic. I still had to test on a real phone, decide what feels fun, and catch things it got wrong. But it let one person ship something that would normally take a team.  
Happy to answer questions about the workflow, what worked and what didn't. I'd also love feedback on the game: what would you want in a coaster builder, and which world should I expand next?

**App Store:** [https://apps.apple.com/app/rideforge/id6826920885](https://apps.apple.com/app/rideforge/id6826920885)  
(iPhone only for now.)
